title: Whole strict-tower comparison for native compact support
statement: Let l be prime and invertible in a field K₀, E a finite extension of Q_l, X and Y finite-type K₀-schemes, f : X → Y a separated finite-type K₀-morphism, and c = (j,p) a compactification. Let SX be any coefficient derived-system calculus on X. Let T and eT be exactly the chosen coherent completed-coefficient tower and its evaluation comparisons from exists_compactSupportReductionTower. Put N = SX.reduction followed by native varying-ring extension by zero along j and derived proper image along p. Let e_n identify the nth finite evaluation of N with finite compact support of the nth scalar reduction, using compactSupportSystemEvaluation and SX.reductionEvaluation. There exists a natural isomorphism α : T ≅ N followed by exact derived restriction to completed-coefficient towers. For every ambient derived K and n, evaluation of α_K, followed by coefficientRestrictedEvaluationIso and restriction of e_n(K), equals eT_n(K). This comparison is an isomorphism of derived strict towers before any total inverse limit; it asserts no recorded integral compact-support action or scalar-adjunction formula.

source.place: Paragraphs 1–2: compatible canonical coefficient comparisons along the whole compact-support quotient tower; precise bridge for the recorded coherent tower

proof.text: Use the normalized flat-term K-flat reduction model in the coefficient calculus to compare SX.reduction with the quotient reduction used in the coherent compact-support tower. Both compute derived extension of coefficients on the entire sequence site, with the universal derived counit and the actual quotient maps. The universal comparison of those left-derived pairs is natural on the unbounded derived category and preserves finite evaluation.

Apply exact sequence-site open extension, separately right-derived proper image, and exact completed-scalar restriction to this whole comparison. Compare with the coherent tower realization by the universal resolution comparisons before evaluation. The recorded geometric evaluation is fixed by the open unit and the proper derived unit. Thus its component after coefficientRestrictedEvaluationIso and the SX finite evaluation is exactly eT_n, giving the displayed normalization. The inverse construction uses the inverse universal comparisons.

lean.statement:
theorem qcqsCompactSupport_nativeTowerComparison
    (SX : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X) :
    let hT := exists_compactSupportReductionTower l E K₀ X Y f hl c
    let T := hT.choose_spec.choose_spec.2.2.choose
    let eT := hT.choose_spec.choose_spec.2.2.choose_spec.2.choose_spec.2.choose
    let N := SX.reduction ⋙ ProEtale.VaryingRing.J (compactSupportSystemLevel l E)
        (compactSupportSystemQuotient l E) c.i ⋙
      ProEtale.VaryingRing.P (compactSupportSystemLevel l E)
        (compactSupportSystemQuotient l E) c.g
    let e (n : ℕ) :=
      Functor.isoWhiskerLeft SX.reduction (compactSupportSystemEvaluation l E c n) ≪≫
        Functor.isoWhiskerRight (SX.reductionEvaluation n)
          (sfIntrinsicCompactSupport c (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
    ∃ α : T ≅ N ⋙ coefficientSequenceDerivedRestriction l E Y,
      ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X)) (n : ℕ),
        (coefficientConstantTowerEvaluation l E Y n).map (α.hom.app K) ≫
            (coefficientRestrictedEvaluationIso l E Y n).hom.app (N.obj K) ≫
            (coefficientFiniteDerivedRestriction l E Y n).map ((e n).hom.app K) =
          (eT n).hom.app K
